derby.coverage: Documented meetings only — {n} in the archives. This is not the full head-to-head history.
derby.wall.empty.title: The wall is bare
derby.wall.empty: The archives hold no scoreline for {club} v {rival} yet. Meetings go up here as research documents them — nothing is filled in by guesswork.
derby.wall.tap: Tap a poster to open its dossier.
derby.dossier.unstated: The archive does not say which side {club} was, so this meeting is listed but not counted in the record.
derby.call.title: Call the derby
derby.call.intro: {n} meetings from the archive. Call each one before the score is shown.
derby.call.rules: Swipe the poster toward your call, or tap a plate. Right calls in a row score more.
derby.call.locked.title: Not enough meetings for a round
derby.call.locked: A round needs {min} meetings whose side the archive states. This rivalry has {n}. The wall and the record stay open.
derby.res.title: Derby slip
derby.share.title: Call the derby
derby.rec.title: Derby record
derby.rec.unstated: {n} listed meeting(s) do not say which side {club} was and are not counted.
derby.rec.undated: {n} counted meeting(s) carry no date and sit outside the decade chart.
derby.lock.title: {mode} is not open yet
derby.lock.meetings: No approved rival is on file for {club} yet, so there is no rivalry to open.
derby.lock.wall: The wall needs {need} approved, distinct names. {club} has {have}. We do not pad a wall to fill it.
derby.lock.blackfile: The Black File needs a sourced, verifiable crossing, or {need2} dated pairs that fall on different exact days. {club} has {have} crossings and {have2} of {need2} pairs.
derby.cov.title: What this covers
derby.cov.line: {n} meetings in the archives we hold · {counted} count toward the record · {dated} carry a date
derby.cov.comps: Competitions as the sources name them: {list}.
derby.cov.shootouts: {n} went to a shoot-out; it is shown apart from the score and never changes the result.
derby.cov.incomplete: This is the documented list, not a complete record of every meeting.
derby.dossier.soLine: {us}–{them} on penalties ({word}). The result above is the score after play.
derby.w.title: Keep one. Tear the other down.
derby.w.intro: {n} duels between two names. Tap the one you would rather keep on the wall; the other comes down.
derby.w.rule.keep: The one you keep stays up and faces the next name.
derby.w.rule.special: Two rounds are marked no mercy.
derby.w.rule.revenge: Once, you may bring back one of the last six you tore down.
derby.w.rule.noScore: It is your preference. Nothing is right or wrong, and nothing is scored.
derby.w.curated: The no-mercy rounds draw their challenger from a curated, editorial ordering of these names. That ordering is the editors’, not the terrace’s.
derby.w.notRanked: No editorial ordering exists for these names, so the no-mercy rounds are dealt like the rest.
derby.w.end.revengeUnused: You did not use your revenge.
derby.w.end.editors: The editors’ ordering puts {name} highest of the names you saw.
derby.w.end.local: A local code for comparing two walls; it does not prove a result.
derby.w.end.preference: These are your preferences. They are not a vote and not a ranking.
derby.w.special.curated: No mercy round: the challenger comes from the editors’ ordering.
derby.w.revenge.title: Bring one back
derby.w.revenge.body: Pick one of the last {n} you tore down. It goes up as the next challenger. You get this once.
derby.bf.title: The Black File
derby.bf.intro: {total} items: {binary} crossings and {pairs} order pairs. Every answer is a documented fact.
derby.bf.rule.direct: “Direct” means straight from one club to the other, with no club in between.
derby.bf.rule.ever: “Ever” allows other clubs in between, in order.
derby.bf.rule.order: Order: pick which of two events came first. Both fall on different, exact days.
derby.bf.rule.denom: Your result counts what was actually asked, with a count for each part.
derby.bf.limited.noCross: Crossings are not open: {club} has {have} sourced, verifiable careers on file.
derby.bf.limited.noOrder: Order pairs: {have2} of {need2}. The file is dealt with the pairs that exist.
derby.bf.q.direct: Did {person} move straight from {from} to {to}, with no club in between?
derby.bf.q.ever: Did {person} get from {from} to {to}, directly or through other clubs in between?
derby.bf.r.why.direct: A sourced move joins the two clubs directly.
derby.bf.r.why.ever: Sourced moves join the two clubs, in order, through the clubs in the path.
derby.bf.r.why.no: The career record we hold for {person} is stated complete, and no path joins the two clubs.
derby.bf.o.why: The earlier event is dated {a}; the later one {b}.
derby.bf.res.title: File closed
derby.bf.err: Could not check that. Try again.
derby.bf.offline: You appear to be offline. Reconnect and try again.
